body.text:
**The board is clear.** Review UI v2 is committed and pushed (`24d4998`), and with it, every item you've asked for is built, verified, and on GitHub.

Run `git for-ai review` now and you'll see your page: **"Ask this repository"** as the hero at the top with suggestion chips and live cited answers; a one-line digest instead of the stat grid; an attention *inbox* grouped by why things need you (unreadable notes first, then low-confidence, inferred, no-intent), each with a plain-English explanation; and a day-grouped, summary-first timeline. Change pages lead with the claim and put the **evidence directly beneath it** — what was tested, and the session that proves it. All the internals (change-ids, provenance enums, full SHAs) are demoted into closed folds rather than deleted, and the footer states the contract you set: agents use `--json`, this page is yours.

**What exists now, three days after "continue our work on this project":**

- A **feature-complete CLI** against its reference — capture, identity that survives rewrites, ledger, semantic index, `ask`/`blame --why` with cited AI answers, `report`, `review`, `sync`, `doctor`, `export`, and the repair tools — 574 tests across four packages, every one exercising real git.
- The **merge-safe JSONL ledger**, **server-free sync** validated against real GitHub, and the **MCP server** making agents native readers and writers of all of it.
- And the proof threaded through everything: this repo is its own best demo. Nearly every commit is agent-authored, self-captured, and interrogable — `git for-ai ask "why is the ledger stored as JSONL?"` will answer from decisions you approved in these very sessions.

Natural next steps when you want them, none urgent: publishing the npm package, the Electron wrapper around the review app, the shared-index server if a second machine ever needs it — and simply using it on a real project that isn't itself. It's been a genuinely good build. Enjoy asking your repo questions.

A proper close-out of the documentation. Plan: archive the executed planning docs (and the original ideas/research) into `architecture/history/`, write a forward-looking `ROADMAP.md`, add `CLAUDE.md` with the working practices this collaboration actually proved out, and refresh the living docs' pointers. Starting with the moves:

Now updating the living docs' references to the moved files:

cd C:/src/git-for-ai && sed -i 's|(architecture/PLAN_2026-07-18\.md)|(architecture/history/PLAN_2026-07-18.md)|g; s|(architecture/MONOREPO_PLAN\.md)|(architecture/history/MONOREPO_PLAN.md)|g; s|(architecture/CLI_PLAN\.md)|(architecture/history/CLI_PLAN.md)|g; s|(ideas/00-overview\.md)|(architecture/history/ideas/00-overview.md)|g; s|(research/landscape\.md)|(architecture/history/research/landscape.md)|g' README.md && sed -i 's|(\./MONOREPO_PLAN\.md)|(./history/MONOREPO_PLAN.md)|g; s|(\.\./research/landscape\.md)|(./history/research/landscape.md)|g; s|(\.\./ideas/00-overview\.md)|(./history/ideas/00-overview.md)|g; s|`\.\./ideas/01`|`./history/ideas/01`|g' architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md && sed -i 's|(\./PLAN_2026-07-18\.md)|(./history/PLAN_2026-07-18.md)|g' architecture/REVIEW_UI.md && grep -c "history/" README.md architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md architecture/REVIEW_UI.md

body.text: Now the README updates — the command table gains the missing commands, and the map points at the new structure:
Now fixing the archived docs' relative links so archaeology still works from their new location:

attributes.command: cd C:/src/git-for-ai/architecture/history && sed -i 's|](\./ARCHITECTURE\.md|](../ARCHITECTURE.md|g; s|](\./DATA_MODEL\.md|](../DATA_MODEL.md|g; s|](\./CLI_REFERENCE\.md|](../CLI_REFERENCE.md|g; s|](\.\./research/|](./research/|g; s|](\.\./ideas/|](./ideas/|g; s|](\./history/|](./|g; s|](architecture/CLI_PLAN\.md)|](./CLI_PLAN.md)|g; s|](architecture/history/|](./|g' *.md && grep -rn "](\.\./ideas\|](\./history/\|](architecture/" *.md | head -5; echo "--- link check done ---"
cd C:/src/git-for-ai/architecture/history && sed -i 's|](architecture/PLAN_2026-07-18\.md)|](./PLAN_2026-07-18.md)|g' HANDOFF_2026-07-17.md && cd ../.. && git add -A && git status --short | head -20

cd C:/src/git-for-ai && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Docs: roadmap, CLAUDE.md, and the archaeology/current split

The documentation now matches the project's actual state — a shipped
v1 — instead of narrating its construction.

- architecture/ROADMAP.md (new): future features in four tiers —
  hardening (npm publish, the never-worked lint, capture enrichment,
  retrieval-quality eval, small flagged debts), proving-it-elsewhere
  (external dogfood, PR-comment recipe, second capture adapter),
  surfaces gated on proven need (Electron wrapper, shared-index
  server, hosted service), and the v2 ideas (drift detector as the
  next novel feature; knowledge graph). Owner-approved decisions from
  the executed plans carried forward and starred.
- CLAUDE.md (new): working context for future agents, distilled from
  how this collaboration actually went — the nine hard rules (real
  git only, non-minting reads, hooks never break commits, JSONL
  writes, honest degradation, package boundaries, the RAM rule,
  scoped API keys, the human/agent audience split), the milestone-
  agent pattern with independent re-verification, the process
  lessons (explicit-path staging, unpiped gate commands, checkpointed
  long runs), owner working style, and Windows quirks.
- Archived: CLI_PLAN, PLAN_2026-07-18, MONOREPO_PLAN, ideas/, and
  research/ all move under architecture/history/ — useful for knowing
  how the project evolved, not needed for new work. Internal links
  fixed for the new locations.
- Living docs updated: README's command table now lists every shipped
  command and the doc map reflects the split; ARCHITECTURE.md's
  status header says Implemented (with the two recorded deviations);
  REVIEW_UI.md carries a shipped-status banner including the v2
  redesign and the humans-only owner direction.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git push origin main "+refs/notes/git-for-ai/*:refs/notes/git-for-ai/*" "+refs/git-for-ai/*:refs/git-for-ai/*" 2>&1 | tail -4 && ls
